title: Prefix cache fingerprinting + cross-request dedupe for prompt-heavy workloads
creator: Samira Patel
description: Goal: Implement a production-safe prefix/prompt cache reuse layer that deduplicates identical prompt prefixes across concurrent and recent requests, reduces duplicated KV-cache materialization on GPUs, and lowers overall GPU memory pressure for tail-heavy prompt workloads. Background: Many customers send repeated prefixes (system prompts, company header, or instruction templates) across requests and sessions. Currently the runtime either re-materializes KV cache per request or keeps short-lived per-process caches that do not dedupe across different request objects or tenants. This leads to duplicated KV tensors occupying GPU memory and repeated compute for the same prefix. Proposed approach: 1) Generate a stable fingerprint for the canonicalized prefix: model id + tokenizer version + normalized token-id sequence + optional tenant namespace salt. Normalization rules remove session-specific placeholders and canonicalize whitespace to maximize dedupe without changing semantics. 2) Use the fingerprint as a key into a shared GPU-resident prefix cache store that maps fingerprint -> serialized KV pages (compressed) + metadata (sequence length, attention mask template, refcount). 3) At batch assembly time, for each incoming request try lookup by fingerprint. On full-hit, attach a lightweight reference to the cached KV pages; on partial-hit (cached shorter prefix), reuse the cached prefix then compute missing suffix and merge. 4) Memory management: maintain per-GPU accounting with refcounts and an LRU eviction. Implement a low-latency decompression path using 8-bit packing + fused memcpy to minimize copy overhead. 5) Consistency and correctness: cache keys are immutable tied to model version + tokenizer hash; cache entries are invalidated on model reloads, tokenizer updates, or explicit rollout. 6) Security & privacy: prefix cache entries must not contain raw PII. We will enforce canonicalization and a soft-PII detector that rejects caching of prefixes flagged for PII. All cached blobs are encrypted at rest and scoped to tenant namespaces unless tenant opts into shared dedupe. Acceptance criteria (see acceptance_criteria field) and performance targets included.
acceptance_criteria: Cache fingerprinting implemented and deterministic across runtime restarts for the same model+tokenizer versions
End-to-end integration with continuous batching: requests with identical prefixes reuse cached KV without recomputation in >=95% of canonical-match cases
Measured P99 generation latency reduced by at least 15% for workloads with >20% prefix repetition compared to baseline
Overall GPU memory footprint for a cilent workload with repeated prefixes reduced by >=20% (measured across 3+ runs)
Automatic invalidation on model or tokenizer change and documented admin controls to flush cache
PII detection prevents caching of flagged prefixes; encryption at rest is verified in unit/integration tests
No regression on streaming use-cases: prefix reuse must be compatible with streaming token emission and KV cache merging
comments: 2026-02-22 - Design sync: Went through canonicalization tradeoffs with Research (Anika) and Security (Ravi). Agreed to use tokenizer ID + byte-hash of token IDs as primary fingerprint component. Avoid storing raw strings in cache. See design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Prefix+Cache+Design

2026-02-28 - Prototype results: Small Python prototype on a 2xA100 dev rig shows dedupe hit-rate improvement from 12% -> 48% on customer-simulated dataset; memory saving ~22% for active KV pages. Benchmark notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-proto-bench

2026-03-03 - Eng code review: PR opened implementing fingerprinting and shared cache shim. Initial implementation uses per-GPU map guarded by spinlock and serialized KV in 16-bit floats. Concern raised by Marco about lock contention under high QPS. Action: switch to lock-free per-shard maps + background compaction (ENG-9472)

2026-03-08 - Security review notes: Ravi flagged PII risk for system prompts that include customer tokens. Decided to add soft-PII detector before caching and per-tenant opt-in for cross-tenant sharing. Security review required: true

2026-03-11 - Perf run on staging: integrated with continuous batching kernel. For sampled workload (100k requests): cache hit-rate 46%, average per-request token compute reduced leading to 18% lower end-to-end cost per token; P99 decode latency improved by 14% on average. Logs and dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/prefix-cache-staging

2026-03-12 - Implementation notes: Changed serialization to 8-bit packed layout to reduce decompression overhead; added refcounting to prevent eviction races. Next: finalize eviction thresholds and memory soft-limits, add unit tests for partial-prefix merging (ENG-9473)
notes: Tradeoffs discussed: aggressive canonicalization increases hit-rate but risks semantic changes for whitespace-sensitive prompts; we choose conservative normalization with a toggle for an aggressive experimental mode. Cross-tenant dedupe default off; enterprise tenants can opt-in for additional savings. We will monitor correctness via golden prompt test-suite and establish a rollback plan tied to rollout flags.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: fingerprint API + canonicalizer + small in-process cache (2 weeks). Phase 2: GPU-resident cache store, 8-bit serialization, per-shard maps, refcounts, eviction (3 weeks). Phase 3: integrate with continuous-batching runtime, partial-prefix merge logic, staging perf runs + canary rollout (2 weeks). Owners: Jorge (lead), Samira (design), Marco (perf kernels), Ravi (security sign-off).
qa_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint determinism, integration tests for full/partial hits, end-to-end perf runs on staging with synthetic and real replayed traces, PII detector test corpus, canary rollout with telemetry and automatic rollback on error budget breach.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: eviction thrashing under bursty load -> mitigation: conservative initial soft-limit and background compaction; implement reference-counted pinning during active batch. Risk: correctness regressions due to tokenizer drift -> mitigation: include tokenizer-hash in fingerprint and force cache flush on tokenizer update. Risk: privacy leakage -> mitigation: PII detection + tenant-scoped entries + encryption.
